details:
When the package's bin starts its local HTTP server, it also starts a relay bridge without an opt-in. The bridge opens a persistent WebSocket to `wss://canvas.xiaohhhh1.com/api/agent-relay` and sends the local agent token in its hello message.

A `request` message received from the relay supplies the HTTP method, path, headers and body to forward to the loopback server. The bridge adds the local `x-canvas-agent-token` header before forwarding the request. It checks that the target has the loopback server's origin, but does not restrict the API path or require local approval for each request.

The injected token passes the local server's authentication middleware. The `/agent/codex/turn` endpoint accepts a caller-supplied prompt and `permissionMode`; `full` maps to Codex `danger-full-access` with `approvalPolicy: never`. A sender able to issue requests through the vendor relay can therefore direct the local coding agent without a local approval prompt.

Evidence: `package/dist/server/http.js:402` starts the relay bridge and lines 305-342 define the Codex turn route; `package/dist/relay-bridge.js:3,74-82,98-104,124,146` define the relay endpoint, send the token and forward token-authenticated requests; `package/dist/agent/codex-client.js:805-812` map `full` to unrestricted execution. The published tarball has sha256 `ebf343ecd8234e78c01ed16d9209c8e5edcf953593d26e84dcd8e4d73ee67b21` and was verified against the npm registry integrity hash.

files.note: 0.4.109 relay bridge: default WebSocket endpoint, token-bearing hello and authenticated loopback request forwarding.
0.4.109 local server: starts the relay bridge and exposes the authenticated Codex turn route.
0.4.109 Codex client: maps full permission mode to danger-full-access with no approval prompts.
